topic: We had hoped to see the northern lights
title: We had hoped to see the northern lights
pt: Foco da aula: past perfect: expectativas não realizadas (had hoped to / had planned to)

lines.en: Look at this snow, Theo! It reminds me of Iceland. We had hoped to see the northern lights there, remember?
lines.pt: Olha essa neve, Theo! Lembra a Islândia. Tínhamos esperado ver a aurora boreal lá, lembra?

lines.en: Of course. We had planned the whole trip around them, but the sky stayed overcast for six nights.
lines.pt: Claro. Tínhamos planejado a viagem toda em torno dela, mas o céu ficou nublado por seis noites.

lines.en: I had checked the forecast every day. I had even hoped to take a photo for my mother.
lines.pt: Eu tinha conferido a previsão todo dia. Até tinha esperado tirar uma foto para a minha mãe.

lines.en: And I had saved money for months. We had booked a tour that promised a guaranteed sighting, which was a mistake.
lines.pt: E eu tinha economizado por meses. Tínhamos reservado um passeio que prometia a aurora garantida, o que foi um erro.

lines.en: I felt let down. The guide had said the chances were high, but nobody had mentioned the clouds.
lines.pt: Fiquei decepcionada. O guia tinha dito que as chances eram altas, mas ninguém tinha mencionado as nuvens.

lines.en: To be fair, we had expected too much. I had read so many reviews that I had imagined a perfect sky.
lines.pt: Para ser justo, tínhamos esperado demais. Eu tinha lido tantas avaliações que imaginei um céu perfeito.

lines.en: True. We had hoped to stay a week, but we had already spent half our budget by the third day.
lines.pt: Verdade. Tínhamos esperado ficar uma semana, mas já tínhamos gastado metade do orçamento no terceiro dia.

lines.en: Still, the trip was not a disaster. We had never seen a glacier before, and that was unforgettable.
lines.pt: Mesmo assim, a viagem não foi um desastre. Nunca tínhamos visto uma geleira antes, e foi inesquecível.

lines.en: You are right. By the time we left, I had stopped thinking about the lights and started enjoying the quiet.
lines.pt: Você tem razão. Quando partimos, eu já tinha parado de pensar na aurora e começado a curtir o silêncio.

lines.en: Then let’s try again next winter. This time we had better check the weather before we book anything.
lines.pt: Então vamos tentar de novo no próximo inverno. Desta vez é melhor checar o tempo antes de reservar qualquer coisa.

lines.en: Maybe the lights had been waiting for us to give up, and they will appear when we stop expecting them.
lines.pt: Talvez a aurora estivesse esperando a gente desistir, e apareça quando pararmos de esperar.

facts.label: Past perfect
facts.sub: Expectativa que falhou: We had hoped to see the lights. Ação anterior: I had checked the forecast. Experiência nova: We had never seen a glacier.

facts.label: Tinha esperado
facts.sub: Use had hoped to + verbo base para uma expectativa que não se realizou: We had hoped to see the lights. O ouvinte entende que não aconteceu. Na fala vira we’d hoped.

facts.label: Tinha planejado
facts.sub: Parecido com hoped: We had planned to stay a week. Mostra o plano antigo. Normalmente vem com but para dizer o que mudou: but we ran out of money.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Had hoped to mostly shows an expectation that did not come true.
We can say “We had never seen a glacier before”.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Had hoped to mostly shows an expectation that did not come true. → Verdadeiro (Yes, often.)
Past perfect uses was + particípio. → Falso (It uses had + particípio.)
We can say “We had never seen a glacier before”. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

paragraphs: It is a snowy morning in Boston. Dawn and Theo are drinking coffee by the window. The snow reminds them of an old trip. Two winters ago, they travelled to Iceland. They wanted to see the northern lights. Things did not go as planned.

“Look at this snow, Theo! It reminds me of Iceland. We had hoped to see the northern lights there, remember?” says Dawn. “Of course. We had planned the whole trip around them, but the sky stayed overcast for six nights.” says Theo. “I had checked the forecast every day. I had even hoped to take a photo for my mother.” says Dawn.
